title: Structure of the exceptional inverse image of the zero section
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ and use the affine-line datum of
[def-pur-affine-line-datum]: $Y$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme,
$e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$, $N=n/e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)$,
$X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $s:Y\hookrightarrow X$ is the zero section,
$j:U=\mathbf G_{m,Y}\hookrightarrow X$ is its open complement, and
$\kappa(t)\in H^1(U,A(1))$ is the coefficient-extended Kummer class
of the coordinate. Work on the small pro-etale sites as in those
conventions, with cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves],
supported cohomology [def-pur-support-cohomology], and
$D^b_{ctf}$ as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Then:

1. The object $Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]$ lies in
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ and is concentrated in degree zero after the
displayed shift, with lisse rank-one cohomology sheaf.
1. Under the long exact sequence of
[thm-pur-with-support-exactness] for the pair
$(s(Y),\mathbf A^1_Y)$, there is a canonical identification
$$
\Gamma\!\left(Y,\mathcal H^0\bigl(Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\bigr)\right)
\cong H^2_{s(Y)}\bigl(\mathbf A^1_Y,\Lambda(1)\bigr),
$$
via which the boundary of the
Kummer class of $t$ corresponds
to an element of the space of morphisms
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Y,\Lambda)}\bigl(\Lambda_Y,Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\bigr).
$$

proof.text: Use the finite stage of [def-pur-conventions] and the exceptional functor with the domains of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Set $p:X\to Y$, $\pi=pj$ and $F=A_X(1)[0]$, with the pair $(s,j)$ and $\kappa(t)$ of [def-pur-affine-line-datum]. Its $e\mid n$ gives $N=n/e\geq1$, and [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level] identifies $A$ as a module with $(\mathbf Z/\ell^N\mathbf Z)^{ef}$, so $A$ is finite. Apply [lem-pur-affine-line-support-geometry] to the underlying finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$. It says that $Y,X,U$ are Noetherian, that $X,U$ are finite type over $k$, and that $j$ is quasi-compact. These are the support and closed-exactness hypotheses needed below.

source.place: first paragraph: affine-line datum; hypotheses of the closed-support construction made explicit

proof.text: In this step write $R s^!_0$ for the right derived functor of $M\mapsto s^{-1}\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ on $D^+$, as specified in [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle], and put $B_0=R s^!_0F$. This notation distinguishes it from the exceptional inverse image defined by etale transport; their comparison will be proved in step 7, after computing $B_0$. The localization lemma applies because $j$ is quasi-compact, $A$ is finite, and $F$ is a sheaf in degree zero. It gives a distinguished triangle $s_*B_0\to F\to Rj_*j^*F\to(s_*B_0)[1]$, with its first arrow the support-adjunction counit. By [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], $s_*$ is exact. On a complex this exactness gives $\mathcal H^q(s_*L)=s_*\mathcal H^q(L)$, since kernels and images commute with an exact functor. Hence $s_*$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and the comparison from its termwise functor to $Rs_*$ is an isomorphism. The termwise functor is triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Apply $Rp_*$ to the triangle: [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] gives preservation of triangles and shifts. This is the finite-level functor of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], constructed by K-injectives, which exist by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the larger-universe small skeletons of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The finite-level composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], with $ps=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $pj=\pi$, identify $Rp_*s_*$ with the identity and $Rp_*Rj_*$ with $R\pi_*$. Thus, with $P=Rp_*F$ and $Q=R\pi_*A(1)_U$, we obtain $B_0\to P\xrightarrow{r}Q\xrightarrow{\delta}B_0[1]$. Here $r$ is derived restriction from $F\to Rj_*j^*F$. No exceptional-functor comparison is used to obtain this triangle.

source.place: first paragraph through the distinguished triangle on Y

proof.text: By [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer](1), the unit $A_Y(1)[0]\to P$ is an isomorphism. By (2), the restriction of this unit along $j$ is the unit $A_Y(1)\to\mathcal H^0(Q)$ and is an isomorphism; this is exactly the equivalence with restriction composed with $p^*$ stated in that clause. Hence $\mathcal H^0(r)$ is an isomorphism. The same proposition gives $\mathcal H^1(Q)\cong A_Y$, with $1$ sent to the edge image of $\kappa(t)$, and $\mathcal H^m(Q)=0$ for $m\geq2$. There is also no negative cohomology of $P$ or $Q$: [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative](1),(2) represents either input sheaf by a K-injective resolution zero below degree zero, and direct image applied termwise remains zero there. The module category is Grothendieck by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] supplies enough injectives. Thus $P$ has cohomology only in degree zero and $Q$ only in degrees zero and one.

source.place: first paragraph: units, Kummer generator, and all vanishing degrees

proof.text: Use [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] on the triangle of step 2. For $m<0$, the exact segment $\mathcal H^{m-1}(Q)\to\mathcal H^m(B_0)\to\mathcal H^m(P)$ has zero outer terms, so $\mathcal H^m(B_0)=0$. In degrees zero and one the exact segment is $0\to\mathcal H^0(B_0)\to\mathcal H^0(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^0(Q)\to\mathcal H^1(B_0)\to0$, giving $\mathcal H^0(B_0)=\mathcal H^1(B_0)=0$. Next, $0=\mathcal H^1(P)\to\mathcal H^1(Q)\xrightarrow{\delta^1}\mathcal H^2(B_0)\to\mathcal H^2(P)=0$ makes $\delta^1$ an isomorphism. For $m\geq3$, again $\mathcal H^{m-1}(Q)=\mathcal H^m(P)=0$, hence $\mathcal H^m(B_0)=0$. Therefore $\mathcal H^2(B_0)\cong A_Y$ via $\delta^1$, and all its other cohomology sheaves vanish. The argument uses kernels and images in the abelian category of module sheaves, not a conclusion from constant numerical ranks.

source.place: first paragraph: displayed long exact sequence and degree-by-degree computation

proof.text: Put $C_0=B_0[2]=R s^!_0A_X(1)[2]$. By [lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift], $\mathcal H^m(C_0)=\mathcal H^{m+2}(B_0)$, so only $\mathcal H^0(C_0)$ survives, and step 4 identifies it with the constant rank-one module sheaf $A_Y$. Apply [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] with $r=0$ to obtain $C_0\cong\mathcal H^0(C_0)[0]\cong A_Y[0]$. The canonical identification with its degree-zero cohomology uses the good-truncation maps: for a representative $C_0^\bullet$, the maps $\tau_{\leq0}C_0^\bullet\to C_0^\bullet$ and $\tau_{\leq0}C_0^\bullet\to\mathcal H^0(C_0)[0]$ induce the identity on degree-zero cohomology and isomorphisms on all other (zero) cohomology groups, hence are quasi-isomorphisms. These are the truncations of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]: the second map is the quotient $\ker d^0\to\ker d^0/\operatorname{im}d^{-1}$ in degree zero and zero in negative degrees. Both maps are natural in chain maps and induce the identity on $\mathcal H^0$; the resulting isomorphism in the derived category is therefore the canonical one and does not use a chosen trivialization $\mathcal H^0(C_0)\cong A_Y$. Thus $C_0$ is concentrated in degree zero, with constant, and in particular lisse, rank-one cohomology.

source.place: end of first paragraph: displayed shift and constant cohomology; canonical good truncation as in Stacks 08J5

proof.text: The constant finite module sheaf $A_Y$ is constructible by the single stratum $Y$ in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Moreover $A_Y[0]$ itself is K-flat in the definition of [def-weil-derived-tensor]: tensoring it with any acyclic complex is that same complex, by the mutually inverse degreewise maps $a\otimes x\mapsto ax$ and $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. Consequently for every degree-zero module sheaf $M$, $C_0\otimes_A^L M\cong A_Y[0]\otimes_A M[0]\cong M[0]$. This proves Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Together with step 5 it proves $C_0\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. The Tor conclusion comes from the explicit tensor unit, and is not deduced from bounded constructibility. This proves the constructibility and Tor claims for the support value $C_0$, before any comparison with the separately defined exceptional inverse image.

source.place: end of first paragraph: constructibility and finite Tor amplitude, with tensor-unit verification

proof.text: Compare $B_0$ with $B=Rs^!F$. The zero section is a closed immersion in the affine-line datum, $X,Y$ are finite type over $k$ and $j$ is quasi-compact by step 1, and $F=A_X(1)[0]$ is bounded below. Steps 5-6 give $B_0=C_0[-2]\cong A_Y[-2]$, which is bounded constructible by [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Thus [lem-pur-closed-support-exceptional-comparison], applied to $i=s$ and $K=F$, gives a canonical isomorphism $\phi:B_0\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ with $\epsilon\circ s_*\phi=\epsilon_0$, where $\epsilon_0$ is the support counit and $\epsilon$ the relative exceptional counit. Put $C=B[2]$. The isomorphism $\phi[2]:C_0\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ carries the concentration, constant rank-one cohomology and finite-Tor conclusions of steps 5-6 to $C$, proving (1). The comparison lemma uses only the full bounded-below etale-origin class; no ambient adjunction on arbitrary pro-etale objects is invoked.

source.place: first paragraph: comparison of the localization support value with the exceptional inverse image, after the relative A1/Gm calculation; expanded relative-adjunction argument

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-supported-hom] to $s$, $F=A_X(1)[0]$, and $a=2$. It gives the natural isomorphism
$$H^2_{s(Y)}(X,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)}(s_*A_Y,F[2]).$$
The support adjunction of [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle], applied to the bounded-below test object $A_Y[-2]$ and input $F$, gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(s_*A_Y,F[2])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(s_*(A_Y[-2]),F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(A_Y[-2],B_0)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(A_Y,C_0).$$
The first and last identifications apply the mutually inverse shift functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; exact termwise $s_*$ commutes with them by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Now compose with postcomposition by $\phi[2]$ from step 7 to obtain $H^2_{s(Y)}(X,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(A_Y,C)$ for the actual exceptional value $C=Rs^!F[2]$. The equality $\epsilon\,s_*\phi=\epsilon_0$ proved in step 7 says exactly that this composite uses the relative exceptional adjunction on the test object $A_Y[-2]$. This establishes the claimed comparison without treating the ambient support adjoint as the transported exceptional functor.

source.place: second paragraph: supported cohomology to the Hom of the actual exceptional value, using the proved counit-compatible comparison

proof.text: Step 7 and the canonical degree-zero truncation of step 5 identify $C$ with $\mathcal H^0(C)[0]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Y,A)}(A_Y[0],C)$ is therefore $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Mod}(A_Y)}(A_Y,\mathcal H^0(C))$. Evaluation at $1$ identifies this last group with $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^0(C))$: a global section $v$ defines on each site object $V$ the $A_Y(V)$-linear map $a\mapsto a\,v|_V$, compatible with restrictions. Conversely, an $A_Y$-linear sheaf map sends $1|_V$ to the restriction of its value at the global section $1$, and hence sends every $a\in A_Y(V)$ to $a$ times that restriction. These constructions are inverse, including on disconnected objects of the site. Composing the inverse of step 8 with this identification gives the claimed canonical isomorphism $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^0(C))\cong H^2_{s(Y)}(X,A(1))$. The class $\kappa(t)$ of [def-pur-affine-line-datum] is a class in $H^1(U,A(1))$, and the pro-etale finite-torsion clause of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] supplies its boundary $\beta=\partial\kappa(t)\in H^2_{s(Y)}(X,A(1))$. Apply the isomorphism of step 8 to $\beta$ to obtain a morphism $A_Y\to C$; under evaluation at $1$ it corresponds to the inverse image of $\beta$ in $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^0(C))$. This proves precisely the asserted correspondence of the boundary class. The statement asks for this correspondence, not for a further equality with a separately constructed Cartier class.

source.place: second paragraph: global sections, supported boundary, and the resulting morphism

proof_origin.place: current blueprint localization and relative A1/Gm argument; support and exceptional values distinguished until the explicit relative-adjunction comparison in step 7

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\Lambda=A$, and let
$s:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y$ be the zero section. Then:

1. The object $Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]$ lies in
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ and is concentrated in degree zero after the
displayed shift, with lisse rank-one cohomology sheaf.
1. Under the long exact sequence of
[thm-pur-with-support-exactness] for the pair
$(s(Y),\mathbf A^1_Y)$, there is a canonical identification
$$
\Gamma\!\left(Y,\mathcal H^0\bigl(Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\bigr)\right)
\cong H^2_{s(Y)}\bigl(\mathbf A^1_Y,\Lambda(1)\bigr),
$$
via which the boundary of the
Kummer class of $t$ corresponds
to an element of the space of morphisms
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Y,\Lambda)}\bigl(\Lambda_Y,Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\bigr).
$$

proof.text:
Write $p:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$, $j:\mathbf G_{m,Y}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y$
and $\pi=pj$ as in [def-pur-affine-line-datum]. Apply the localization
triangle of [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle] for the closed–open
pair $(s,j)$ and $K=\Lambda(1)_{\mathbf A^1_Y}$, whose first term is
built from the exceptional inverse image of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image],
$$
s_*Rs^!\Lambda(1)\longrightarrow\Lambda(1)\longrightarrow
Rj_*j^*\Lambda(1)\xrightarrow{+1},
$$
and then the triangulated functor $Rp_*$ of
[def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Since $s_*$ is exact,
$Rp_*s_*=R(ps)_*=\operatorname{id}$, and $Rp_*Rj_*=R\pi_*$ by the
composition of derived direct images
[lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], this gives a
distinguished triangle on $Y$
$$
Rs^!\Lambda(1)\longrightarrow Rp_*\Lambda(1)\xrightarrow{\ j^*\ }
R\pi_*\Lambda(1)\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }Rs^!\Lambda(1)[1].
$$
By [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer](1) the middle term is $\Lambda_Y(1)$ in
degree $0$, via the unit of $p$. By [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer](2),(3)
the right-hand term has $\mathcal H^0=\Lambda_Y(1)$ via the unit of
$\pi$, $\mathcal H^1$ free of rank one on $\kappa(t)$, and no other
cohomology sheaves. By [fix-prop-adjunctions](3) the unit of $\pi$ is
$j^*$ composed with the unit of $p$, so $\mathcal H^0(j^*)$ is an
isomorphism. The long exact sequence of cohomology sheaves
$$
0\to\mathcal H^0(Rs^!\Lambda(1))\to R^0p_*\Lambda(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}
R^0\pi_*\Lambda(1)\to\mathcal H^1(Rs^!\Lambda(1))\to R^1p_*\Lambda(1)=0
\to R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1)\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }\mathcal H^2(Rs^!\Lambda(1))
\to R^2p_*\Lambda(1)=0\to\cdots
$$
therefore gives $\mathcal H^m(Rs^!\Lambda(1))=0$ for $m\neq2$ (for
$m\geq3$ it sits between $R^{m-1}\pi_*\Lambda(1)=0$ and
$R^mp_*\Lambda(1)=0$), and an isomorphism
$$
\delta:\ \Lambda_Y\cdot\kappa(t)=R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\mathcal H^2(Rs^!\Lambda(1))=\mathcal H^0\bigl(Rs^!\Lambda(1)[2]\bigr).
$$
So $Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]$ is concentrated in degree zero,
with cohomology sheaf the constant sheaf $\Lambda_Y$, free of rank one on
the boundary $\delta\kappa(t)$; in particular it is lisse of rank one,
constructible, and of finite Tor amplitude, i.e. it lies in
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Constancy is read off from the triangle; it is
not inferred from constancy of ranks.

For the second assertion, the support identification
[lem-amb-closed-support-hom] identifies
$H^2_{s(Y)}(\mathbf A^1_Y,\Lambda(1))$ with
$\operatorname{Hom}_Y(\Lambda_Y,Rs^!\Lambda(1)[2])$.
Since the target is concentrated in degree zero, this Hom group is
$\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^0(Rs^!\Lambda(1)[2]))$.
The boundary of the coordinate class in
[def-pur-affine-line-datum], [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]
is precisely the supported Cartier morphism of
[lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]; the latter construction also gives
its compatibility with base change of this zero-section pair.
